subject: Logic
title: Church-Turing Thesis
description: A short lesson to help you apply Church-Turing Thesis.

hook.text: Before computers existed, two men independently defined what computation is—and arrived at the same answer.

buildup.text: Alonzo Church used lambda calculus. Alan Turing used abstract machines. Both captured the same concept.

discovery.text: The Church-Turing thesis: anything computable by any method can be computed by a Turing machine.

twist.text: It's not technically a theorem—it can't be formally proved. But no counterexample has ever been found.

climax.text: Every computer, phone, and server runs on this foundation. Computation has one universal boundary.

punchline.text: All computers are the same computer, deep down.

quiz.question: What does the Church-Turing thesis state?
options: Anything computable can be computed by a Turing machine
